name: m5-persistent
description: Persistent tables (one per thread for the whole fork, as a resident compiler such as dotc's `ContextBase.uniques` would keep) under a small young generation: 2 GB heap, `-Xmn256m`, 4 MB regions, so the table lives through hundreds of young GCs and its chunks tenure. Dead entries leave the table only after reference processing clears them, which for a tenured element waits on old-generation marking, so the table grows and inserts dirty cards in old regions.

Asks: how far the weak tables diverge once the table outlives compiles, and whether rejuvenation (`-rejuv`) or dropping the queue (`-lazy`) helps there. Strong tables cannot persist. Graal 25.4.4 on the M5 Pro, one fork per table and round.

variantDescriptions.chunked-weak-rejuv: `chunked-weak`, copying each element chunk written at least 256 times since the last GC, so chunks stay young
